key_insight: Canonical lifted-product codes let high-rate qLDPC codes support a complete, modular logical gate set by organizing logical operators into a symmetry-based canonical basis.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical path to low-overhead fault-tolerant computation on dense quantum memories, reducing the need for code-agnostic surgery and teleportation methods.
method: Exploit cyclic symmetry to define a canonical logical basis for lifted-product codes.
Construct constant-depth logical Clifford operations via automorphisms and fold-transversal gates.
Build modular graph-code surgery, parallel Pauli-product measurement, and magic-state injection from reusable seed gadgets or a compact extractor.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports concrete example codes such as [[1122,148,≤20]] and [[4350,1224,≤20]], requiring only a small number of seed gadgets or an extractor smaller than half the data block.
watch_item: The approach is tailored to canonical cyclic-symmetry LP codes, so hardware mapping and circuit compilation may be less straightforward for non-canonical codes or architectures with limited parallelism.
paper_title: Logical computation with canonical lifted product codes
